Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Early Stage NSCLC (Stage I and II)
Required findings: Patient must be medically inoperable or refuse surgery.
Tumor must be node-negative (N0).
Tumor must be peripheral.

Non-Indications: Patients with hilar nodal involvement (should be treated with standard fractionation, e.g., 60 Gy in 6 weeks, rather than SBRT).
Patients with central tumors, as they can experience excessive toxicity when higher fraction sizes and fewer fractions (e.g., 3) are utilized.
Patients who are surgically operable and do not refuse surgery (SBRT is specified for those medically inoperable or who refuse surgery).
Patients with node-positive disease (SBRT is specified for node-negative stage I and stage II).
Important criteria & exceptions: SBRT is generally delivered in 3 to 5 fractions.
Image-guided radiation therapy (IGRT) may be used to improve the therapeutic ratio by eliminating additional margins for daily set-up variability.
Use of mediastinoscopy is appropriate for staging of clinical stage T2N0 patients prior to definitive SBRT.

Staging workup confirming node-negative (N0) status.
Mediastinoscopy report for clinical stage T2N0 patients.
Imaging confirming tumor is peripheral and less than 5 cm in maximum dimension.
